# MDM Rollout Plan

**Owner:** Sam Whitfield · **Status (Oct 8):** 65 of 68 laptops enrolled (96%). Target 100% by 2026-10-17.

## Why

The Information Security Policy requires every company laptop that can reach company systems to be managed: disk encryption on, screen lock, OS updates within 14 days, remote wipe. Until July we enforced this by asking nicely. SOC 2 Type II needs proof it's true for every device, every day of the observation window.

## Fleet

| Type | Count |
|---|---|
| macOS, employee | 62 |
| macOS, contractor (company-issued) | 4 |
| Linux workstations (engineering) | 2 |
| **Total** | **68** |

Contractors on personal machines don't get production access. That rule is in the access review.

## Baseline policy pushed by MDM

- FileVault on, recovery key escrowed
- Firewall on
- Screen lock after 5 minutes
- OS updates: install within 14 days of release, forced at 21
- Gatekeeper on; no unsigned kernel extensions
- Remote lock and wipe enabled
- Endpoint agent for malware detection
- Device posture check before SSO: non-compliant devices can't sign in to production tools

## Phases

| Phase | Dates | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Pilot | Jul 20-31 | Security, Payments | 11 devices, 2 policy tweaks |
| 2. Engineering | Aug 3-21 | All engineering macOS | Slower than planned; ACH cut-over week |
| 3. Company | Aug 24 - Sep 11 | Everyone else | 60 of 68 by Sep 10 |
| 4. Stragglers | Sep 14 - Oct 17 | Remaining 8 | 65 of 68 by Oct 8 |
| 5. Enforcement | From 100% | Posture check blocks SSO | |

## Progress

| Date | Enrolled | % |
|---|---|---|
| Jul 31 | 11 | 16% |
| Aug 21 | 39 | 57% |
| Sep 10 | 60 | 88% |
| Sep 25 | 63 | 93% |
| Oct 8 | 65 | 96% |

## Remaining three

1. **Two Linux engineering workstations.** The macOS MDM doesn't manage Linux. We're using the endpoint agent plus a configuration baseline enforced by a script, with posture reported to the SSO check. Agent installed on one; second scheduled Oct 13.
2. **One laptop belonging to an employee on leave** until Oct 14. Enrollment booked for their first morning back. Until then the device is blocked from SSO.

## Exceptions

None granted. A request to exempt one Linux workstation was declined; the alternative baseline is good enough for the control.

## What went wrong

- I underestimated how long enrollment takes when people are busy. Phase 2 overlapped the ACH cut-over and the investing beta prep. Engineers deferred the restart prompt for days.
- The first enrollment email looked like phishing. Several people correctly reported it. Next time: announce in all-hands first.

## Decisions

Decision: posture checks start blocking SSO for non-compliant devices once we reach 100%, not before. Blocking at 96% would lock out the person on leave and the Linux users.

Decision: new hires get pre-enrolled machines from day one (Engineering Onboarding Guide updated).

Risk: the control has to hold for the whole Type II window. A device that drops out of compliance in November is an exception even if we hit 100% in October.

## Actions

- [x] Sam: pilot and policy baseline by 2026-07-31
- [x] Sam: engineering enrollment by 2026-08-21
- [ ] Sam: second Linux workstation onboarded to the agent baseline by 2026-10-13
- [ ] Sam: enroll the returning employee's laptop by 2026-10-14
- [ ] Sam: MDM at 100% and posture enforcement on by 2026-10-17
- [ ] Sam: weekly compliance report into the SOC 2 evidence folder by 2026-10-23
